entries.title: The Gift
entries.summary: Explains the social penalty of The Gift on mundane people and animals, how Gentle and Blatant Gifts differ, how familiarity and Parma Magica change it, and its effect on supernatural creatures.
quotes: she suffers a -3 penalty to any die rolls she must make
she suffers a –6 penalty to any die rolls she must make
The Parma Magica blocks these effects of The Gift entirely.

entries.title: The Gift: First Impressions
entries.summary: Examples of how villagers, innkeepers, monks and covenant guards react to strangers with no Gift or a Gentle Gift, a Gift, or a Blatant Gift.
quotes: Blatant Gift: The villagers tell the characters to get out of the village

entries.title: The Gift: Established Relationships
entries.summary: Examples of how innkeepers and monks treat a magus they already know well, depending on whether the magus has a Gentle Gift, a Gift or a Blatant Gift.

entries.title: Reputations
entries.summary: A Reputation has a score, a content and a type (Local, Ecclesiastical or Hermetic). To see whether someone has heard of a character, roll a stress die plus the Reputation against an Ease Factor set by distance; a bigger success means more is known.
quotes: A random person has heard of a character with a Reputation if a roll of a stress die plus the Reputation equals or exceeds the Ease Factor given on the table below.

entries.title: Reputation Ease Factors
entries.summary: A table of Ease Factors for being known, by Reputation type and how far away the listener is (village to country, parish to whole Church, covenant to whole Order).

entries.title: The Simple System, From the Core Rulebook
entries.summary: Recaps the core wealth system in which wealth is relative to social class and set by Social Status and Virtues and Flaws, and how fiefs gain value as story rewards.
quotes: a character's level of wealth is an effect of social status, modified by Virtues and Flaws like Wealthy or Poor

entries.title: The Mythic Pound System, From Covenants
entries.summary: Recaps the Mythic Pound accounting system and applies it to a knight's manor, breaking down his expenses, surplus and income, and the cost of knight service.
quotes: Each Mythic Pound can be divided into 20 shillings or 240 pence.
assume that a knight makes ten pounds each year for each manor that does not owe knight service.

entries.title: Folk Ken
entries.summary: Folk Ken lets a character read another person's background and motives, with the storyguide often rolling in secret so the player does not know the result.
quotes: Often the storyguide secretly rolls a die when this Ability is used.

entries.title: Guile
entries.summary: Guile covers lying, feigning and disguise, often as an opposed roll; understanding the target gives a bonus.
quotes: roll 9+ on Perception + Folk Ken
It is often an opposed roll, against the victim's Perception + Folk Ken or, for disguise, Perception + Awareness.

entries.title: Nepotism
entries.summary: Optional use of family members as agents: the player links story events to their fortunes so Bond Maintenance points from adventure experience can be spent on them.
quotes: This allows the magus to spend Bond Maintenance points, which equal the Adventure experience they receive for the story, on their family members.

entries.title: Agencies Overview
entries.summary: Introduces agencies, networks of mundane contacts through which a principal pursues goals without being implicated in meddling, and defines principals and agents.
quotes: A character controlling an agency is called its principal, in this chapter.
An agent is a person bound to offer assistance to a principal.

entries.title: Agents are Directly Controlled
entries.summary: Gives the formula for the maximum number of agents a principal can directly control, based on Presence, Intrigue or Leadership and the Gift's social penalty, and what happens if it is exceeded.
quotes: Maximum Number of Agents: [2 x (Presence + Intrigue
A character can always control one agent, no matter how poor his social skills or what the penalty of his Gift.

entries.title: Agents Act as Intermediaries (Factors)
entries.summary: Explains that most people commanded through an agency are resources controlled by an agent rather than extra agents, and introduces the factor, a single agent who runs the whole agency using his own statistics.
quotes: An agent employed to control an entire agency on behalf of a magus is called a factor.

entries.title: Designing Agents
entries.summary: Lists the few statistics needed for each agent (name, Social Status, Bond, resources) and the Difficult Underlings problem when a principal controls an agent of higher social standing, with magi exempt.
quotes: A Bond , which is a Personality Trait that expresses the reason that the agent is subordinate to the principal

entries.title: Partial Adoption (Agencies)
entries.summary: Optional approach in which troupes do not convert Virtues and Flaws such as Social Contacts or Close Family Ties into fully described agencies, tracking only agents gained during play.

entries.title: Recruited Agents as Story Rewards
entries.summary: How to recruit an agent during play: impress the prospect with a roll, earn agency experience points from stories to wear down his Resistance Strength to zero, and build a Bond. Also covers inheriting an agency and why agents cannot be bought.
quotes: Impressing a Potential Agent: Presence + Leadership – social penalty of The Gift + stress die vs. Ease Factor 6
It takes the current value of a given Resistance Strength in agency experience points to decrease that strength by one

entries.title: Using Agents
entries.summary: How a principal sets agents tasks: a Persuasion Roll against an Ease Factor from the Tasks for Agents table, then a roll or side story for the task itself. Covers using agents for information or assistance and limits on how often they can be asked.
quotes: Persuasion Roll: Communication + Charm, Intrigue, or Leadership + Bond Strength – social penalty of The Gift + stress die vs. Ease Factor (see table under Tasks for Agents)

related.text: Modifiers to Persuasion Roll Ease Factors

entries.title: Resistance of Agents (rules)
entries.summary: Explains Resistance Strength, an agent's reluctance to serve, how it is reduced to zero and how the Bond Strength then grows, with a cap, and notes that Hermetic magi are never agents.
quotes: to a maximum of +6, representing a fanatically dedicated agent

entries.title: Confounding Situations
entries.summary: Guidance on how often an agent's Flaws make him unavailable to the principal, and how the Difficult Underlings Story Flaw applies to a whole agency.
quotes: an agent with a Minor Flaw might be unable to help his principal once out of every four requests

entries.title: Maintaining Agents
entries.summary: Agencies need upkeep: stories can lower an agent's Bond Strength, and it is raised through favors, which convert Adventure experience into agency experience, or money, which can only raise it up to a limit.
quotes: One Mythic Pound's worth of material goods can take the place of 5 agency experience points (or 4 shillings per point) without need for a story
Bond Strength can never rise above +3 by the application of money

entries.title: Resistance of Agents Table
entries.summary: Tables of base Resistance by Social Status and the modifiers for Flaws, coercion and useful resources, used to cost agents at creation and to set the difficulty of recruiting them. A minimum applies.
quotes: A potential agent's Resistance cannot be less than 1.

entries.title: Tasks for Agents
entries.summary: Table of Ease Factors for the Persuasion Roll to get an agent to supply information or perform an easy, hard or impressive task.

entries.title: Modifiers to Persuasion Roll Ease Factors
entries.summary: Modifiers to a Persuasion Roll Ease Factor for how soon the task must be done and the personal risk to the agent, including the number of botch dice.

entries.title: The Hunt
entries.summary: Why nobles hunt, hunting rights in chases, warrens and forests, poaching, and the etiquette of noble hunting, including that spells making prey fall dead breach etiquette and that hunting sick prey costs Reputation.
quotes: A chase or warren is a Minor Surroundings Boon
Spells that cause the prey to simply fall over dead, or otherwise fail to provide a challenging pursuit, are, however, regarded as a breach of etiquette

entries.title: Varieties of Hunting Hounds
entries.summary: The classes of hunting dog (lymers, running dogs, greyhounds, alaunts, mastiffs, harriers and bird dogs), what each does in a hunt, and the master of kennels who trains them.
quotes: The main classes are lymers, running dogs, greyhounds, alaunts, mastiffs, harriers, and bird dogs.

entries.title: Hunting with Hounds
entries.summary: Introduces the most prestigious form of hunting, whose general format anyone with the Etiquette Ability knows, and which the following stage-by-stage sections detail.
quotes: the general format is known and accepted by anyone with a score in the Ability Etiquette

entries.title: The Quest
entries.summary: First stage of a formal hunt: huntsmen with lymers track and assess prey using a tracking roll, a roll to keep the lymer quiet, and a roll to judge the quarry's age and condition.
quotes: Huntsmen each make Perception + (the lymer's or huntsman's Hunt Ability, whichever is lower) rolls against Ease Factor 9, to track an appropriate beast to its lair.

entries.title: The Assembly
entries.summary: The breakfast at which huntsmen present their finds and guests inspect droppings with a Perception + Hunt test to choose the day's prey.
quotes: These are examined with a test of Perception +Hunt against Ease Factor 12

entries.title: The Relay
entries.summary: Positioning of the running dogs, greyhounds, alaunts and mastiffs in advance along the prey's likely path, using Area Lore and Hunting, and what happens if the dogs are poorly placed.
quotes: Area Lore is essential to understand the lay of the land, and the Ability Hunting to predict the pursued animal's erratic path correctly.

entries.title: The Chase
entries.summary: The core hunt resolution: each hourly round hunters roll to keep up, hounds and prey lose fatigue unless they pass Stamina rolls, and the hounds' Pursuit Total is compared to the prey's Evasion Total to decide who wins each round until one side has won enough rounds.
quotes: Each round of the chase represents one hour of pursuit, and requires a Dexterity + Ride stress roll against Ease Factor 6 to keep in sight of the hounds.
Pursuit Total: Hound's Perception + hound's Hunt + stress die – lowest Fatigue penalty among the hounds vs.
Evasion Total: Prey's Dexterity + Athletics + Terrain Bonus (starts at 6) + stress die – Fatigue penalty

entries.title: The Unmaking and Curee
entries.summary: The formal butchering of the quarry and rewarding of the dogs, with its customs represented by the Hunt Ability, and the note that informal hunts are also common.
quotes: There is a formal set of customs to this, represented by the Hunt Ability

entries.title: Bow and Stable Hunting
entries.summary: A drive hunt with archers and mounted beaters, which takes much game but has lower status than hunting with hounds except in certain Tribunals.
quotes: bow and stable hunting lacks the status of hunting with hounds

entries.title: The Terrain Bonus
entries.summary: A bonus added to the prey's Evasion Total when it is native to the terrain, and the per-round rolls by the relay planners and hunters that can reduce it, even turning it into a penalty over a long hunt.
quotes: This is reflected in a Terrain Bonus of +6 added to the prey's Evasion Total.
Every round, any character who participated in establishing the relay must make a stress roll of Intelligence + Hunt + 6 against an Ease Factor equal to the Evasion Total.

entries.title: The Prey
entries.summary: Which animals nobles hunt and when: the preference order from magical animals through Beasts of Virtue to the finest mundane game, the seasons of the hart, boar and bear, and the prestige (or lack of it) of hunting hare, wolf, fox and otter.
quotes: The order of preference for prey begins with powerful, unusual, and exotic magical animals (especially those that offer a great challenge and threaten the estate); continues to Beasts of Virtue; and ends with the very best specimens of mundane animals.

related.text: The Book of Mundane Beasts, Realms of Power: Magic pp.140-144

entries.title: Public Power for Women
entries.summary: Introduces how women gain public power in Mythic Europe, framed as material for storytelling rather than prohibition, and points to the Paid Rights Virtue for exceptional women characters.
quotes: The Paid Rights Virtue (page 100) is a gamemechanical way to acknowledge that an exceptional woman is just that: exceptional.

entries.title: Dressing As A Man
entries.summary: The simplest way for a woman to avoid social conventions: dressing as a man, which may become a Dark Secret and may qualify for Gender Nonconforming.
quotes: This may become a Dark Secret (page 124), and may also qualify the character for Gender Nonconforming (page 131).

entries.title: Holding Land (Women)
entries.summary: The six ways a woman can come to control land (absence, inheritance, political success, conquest, widow's portion, stewardship) with notes on how each works in practice and a rule of thumb for a widow's income.
quotes: Women can gain control of land in six ways: during absence, through inheritance, via political success, through conquest, in a widow's portion, or as a steward.
As a rule of thumb, assume a widow can keep the profit, not income, of a third of her husband's land until she remarries.

entries.title: Public Power for Women
entries.summary: Frames the constraints on women holding public power as storytelling material rather than prohibitions, and notes that women have fewer rights in England than elsewhere in Mythic Europe.
quotes: The constraints, and ways to avoid them, listed here are suggested as material for storytelling, not as proscriptions.

entries.title: Dressing as a Man
entries.summary: The simplest way for a woman to avoid social conventions, with its practical limits for the long term; it may become a Dark Secret.
quotes: This may become a Dark Secret.

entries.title: Holding Land
entries.summary: Lists the six ways a woman can gain control of land, each of which is then detailed in a subsection.
quotes: Women can gain control of land in six ways: during absence, through inheritance, via political success, through conquest, in a widow's portion, or as a steward.

entries.title: Absence
entries.summary: How a noblewoman acts as deputy while her husband is away: her Abilities, her right to spend the income and command vassals, her role in siege defense and her networks of agents.
quotes: Women raised for this task always have Leadership and Profession: Steward scores.

entries.title: Inheritance
entries.summary: How women inherit land in different parts of Europe, whether they keep legal authority in marriage, and how dowry land relates to inheritance.
quotes: A woman who rules a fief by inheritance usually retains legal authority in it during her marriage.

entries.title: Widow's Portion and Stewardship
entries.summary: A rule of thumb for how much of her late husband's land a widow can keep and when she regains full ownership of her own lands.
quotes: As a rule of thumb, assume a widow can keep the profit, not income, of a third of her husband's land until she remarries.

entries.title: Nuns
entries.summary: The Church as a third avenue of power for women: nuns' legal status, their land, temporary vows and the use of nunneries as refuge.
quotes: Nuns are considered wards of the bishop, and brides of Christ.

entries.title: Control Through Emotional Bonds
entries.summary: Introduces an optional network-of-influence system, adapted from other supplements, to model unexpected loyalties between noble allies whose tight emotional bonds make them act against their apparent interests. Troupes decide how far to use it.
quotes: The rules in this section are used to model the unexpected interactions between people whose tight emotional bonds make them do things which, superficially, are not in their own interests.

related.text: Merchant houses and magi's private agents (other supplements)

entries.title: Agents
entries.summary: Defines agents as directly controlled subordinates, gives the formula for how many a principal may have, and lists who does not count as an agent (magi, colorful characters, indirect subordinates, hirelings and other players' characters). A principal with weak Presence or Leadership can run a network through a single primary agent, called a factor.
quotes: 2 x (Presence + Intrigue or Leadership – social penalty for the Gift) or 1, whichever is larger.

entries.title: Design of Agents
entries.summary: The handful of statistics each agent needs: a name, a Social Status Virtue or Flaw, a Bond expressed as a Personality Trait, and the resources the principal can draw on through the agent. Worked examples show how a vassal and a bishop are built.
quotes: A Bond, which is a Personality Trait that expresses the reason for the agent's attachment to the principal, and its strength.

entries.title: Acquiring Agents
entries.summary: How characters gain agents, either at character creation through certain Virtues or in play by impressing a prospect with a Presence + Leadership roll and then wearing down his resistance with Agency Experience points. Includes the recruitment, task and persuasion tables.
quotes: Each of these virtues grants 12 points to spend on the accompanying Agent Recruitment Table for thematically appropriate agents.
a stress die + Presence + Leadership – social penalty for the Gift against an Ease Factor of 6.
A character's resistance is reduced by 1 in exchange for a number of Agency experience points equal to their current resistance.

entries.title: Agent Recruitment Table
entries.summary: Tables that set a potential agent's starting resistance from his Social Status, then adjust it for circumstances such as inconvenient Flaws and for the resources he can offer the principal.
quotes: A potential agent always has a minimum resistance score of 1.

entries.title: Tasks For Agents Table
entries.summary: Gives the persuasion Ease Factor for common agent tasks such as fetching information or performing easy, hard or impressive deeds, with modifiers for how quickly the task is needed and how much personal risk it carries.
quotes: Perform an Impressive Task (Ease Factor 18 or less).

entries.title: Using Agents
entries.summary: How a principal sets an agent a task with a persuasion roll against the Tasks for Agents table, how the agent then rolls his own Characteristics and Abilities, and how passive information gathering, active information gathering and requests for assistance are treated.
quotes: stress die + Communication + (Charm, Intrigue, or Leadership as situationally appropriate) + Bond Strength – social penalty of the Gift vs. an Ease factor on the Tasks for Agents table

entries.title: Maintaining Agents
entries.summary: How a principal keeps an agent's Bond from waning: by aiding the agent in stories and spending matching Agency experience points on the Bond, or less effectively by paying money.
quotes: A character may buy 5 Agency experience points per pound, and spend them as above to increase the bond of characters.

entries.title: Reputation
entries.summary: Explains how players of nobles use Reputation rolls to estimate the overt traits, interests and resources of other members of the ruling class, and how a Reputation helps in dissuading enemies or in a knight's early career.
quotes: The players of nobles can estimate the overt personality traits, publicly declared interests, and obvious resources of members of their class using Reputation rolls.

entries.title: Noble Reputation
entries.summary: Adds Noble Reputation as a fourth style of Reputation alongside Local, Hermetic and Ecclesiastic, and defines who counts as part of the landed class for these Reputations.
quotes: This section extends the Reputation Table on page 19 of ArM5, providing a fourth style of Reputation to accompany Local, Hermetic, and Ecclesiastic.

entries.title: Prudhomme
entries.summary: Describes the ideal Reputation of a male noble, the prudhomme, and what a knight must be and do to be so regarded.
quotes: A man is a prudhomme if he is noble of blood, handsome, demonstrates prowess, and is of suitable character.

entries.title: Improving Noble Reputation
entries.summary: How a noble acquires a first Noble Reputation by entering feudal life and then raises it by spending seasons on notable deeds or through significant events, using the normal Ability experience table. Lists example activities and bonus experience for events like crusading or gaining a liege.
quotes: Every time a noble spends a season performing great deeds notable to other members of his class, he adds 1 Experience to his reputation.
Gaining a royal liege grants 6 experience points.

entries.title: The Advantages of Reputation
entries.summary: Explains that a strong Reputation lets other nobles judge a character's interests and intentions, so it affects their plans even when he does nothing.
quotes: A fierce Reputation is a potent envoy.

entries.title: Reputation Roll Adjustments
entries.summary: Tables of Ease Factors by distance and of modifiers for the subject's status and circumstances, used when rolling a Noble Reputation to recall what is known about another noble.
quotes: Same shire, county, or equivalent
A commoner in the service of a noble.
A vassal of the character making the roll.

entries.title: Reputation is Utterly Vital
entries.summary: Advice on how nobles use a rival's Reputation to predict willingness to fight, retreat, bargain or change sides, and how single actions change the effect of a Reputation without changing its score, illustrated with the story of William Marshal.
quotes: In neither John nor Stephen's case does the Reputation score fall.

entries.title: Proctors
entries.summary: Proctors represent bishops, nobles or religious houses at the papal curia, presenting and appealing petitions, and are bound by four rules on tenure, concubinage, number per client and substitutes.
quotes: There are four rules for proctors:

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: The Petition Total
entries.summary: The core procedure for getting the Church to act: a Petition Total, built from Communication or Presence plus Church Lore plus modifiers and with no die roll, is compared with an Ease Factor set by the request, with a list of example Ease Factors and rules for who can grant what, written versus audience petitions, and scribes.
quotes: Petition Church: Petition Total vs Petition Ease Factor
Written Petition Total: Com + Church Lore + Modifiers
Audience Petition Total: Pre + Church Lore + Modifiers

related.text: The Church Ch.2 Furthering the cultus

entries.title: Modifiers to the Petition Total
entries.summary: Lists the bonuses and penalties that supporters, donations, arguments based on Abilities, visions, miracles and reputation add to a Petition Total, how an argument is rolled, and which bonuses do not stack.
quotes: Argument Success: Int + Ability Score + stress die vs Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Henri of Toulouse's Petition
entries.summary: A worked example of building a Petition Total for founding a monastery from a scribe's total plus several supporting modifiers.

entries.title: The Petition of the Parish of Long Melford
entries.summary: A second worked example of a Petition Total, for moving a parish's feast days.

entries.title: Acting Without Authority
entries.summary: Sets the highest Ease Factor of petition that a bishop or a priest may grant on his own authority, and notes that such decisions can still be questioned later and that characters may act beyond their authority at some risk.
quotes: A bishop (or equivalently ranked character) may grant any petition or take any action with an Ease Factor of up to 15 without consulting his peers or superiors.

entries.title: Appealing a Petition
entries.summary: An appeal is itself a petition whose Ease Factor to overturn is based on the original Petition Total, with a compromise offered if it falls only slightly short, and a penalty for appealing after the original season.
quotes: Ease Factor to Overturn a Petition: Original Petition Total + 3
Ease Factor to Open Negotiations for Compromise: Original Petition Total – 3
If an appeal is not made in the same season as the original petition, then the appeal has a –3 penalty to its Petition Total.

entries.title: Canon Courts
entries.summary: Explains who judges in the Church's courts, how clergy are shielded from secular justice, what falls under canon jurisdiction, how summons and judgments work, and how compurgation can acquit a defendant on character witnesses.
quotes: A person cannot be forced, except by papal decree, to attend a canon court further than two days travel from his diocese.

entries.title: Punishment
entries.summary: Lists the Church's punishments: excommunication, irregularity (which stops a cleric using Faith Points), monition, public penance, imprisonment in a religious house, fines and suspension of a benefice; canon courts may not impose death or physical punishment.
quotes: An irregular clergyman cannot make use of Faith Points.
An excommunicate character is cursed and receives no benefit from any of the Sacraments except penance

entries.title: Shedding of Blood
entries.summary: Lists what clerics are forbidden to do with regard to bloodshed, including sentencing, attending punishments, commanding fighting men and ordeals, and (for major orders) practising chirurgy.
quotes: Clerics are forbidden to shed blood.
In addition, clerics in major orders may not practice chirurgy.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.78 Ordeals

entries.title: Sanctuary
entries.summary: A church, churchyard and cemetery give fugitives a limited period of sanctuary during which blood may not be spilled.
quotes: Sanctuary is granted for up to 40 days

entries.title: Simony
entries.summary: Buying or selling sacred things is a canon crime; the buyer loses what was gained and the seller is fined and may be excommunicated for repeat offences.
quotes: The seller is fined twice the value of the transaction

entries.title: Sorcery and Witchcraft
entries.summary: Minor sorcery is rarely heard in canon courts and usually earns a public penance, while serious sorcery is prosecuted by secular courts with death as a possible punishment.
quotes: A typical penance involves wearing a white sheet before the congregation

entries.title: The Fine Art of Debate
entries.summary: Introduces the debate rules, which have two parts: testing the strength of each side's position, then converting the result into the opinions of any observers.
quotes: The rules given below present a mechanic for settling an argument through debate.

entries.title: Resolving Differences (Debate Rounds)
entries.summary: The core debate procedure, modelled on certamen: each round the debaters pick an Attack Ability and Defense Ability and compare six totals, with debate fatigue, a table of attack modifiers by tactic and a worked example.
quotes: Attack Total: Communication + Attack Ability + attack modifier + stress die
Defense Total: Intelligence + Defense Ability + stress die
Weakening Total: Presence + Attack Advantage

entries.title: Winning Arguments
entries.summary: How to turn the result of a debate into votes from observers: divide them into factions, compute Argument Strength from Fatigue Levels lost, and read the share of neutral and hostile votes won from a table, with a worked example.
quotes: Argument Strength: Difference between the number of Fatigue Levels lost
If a debate ends because one opponent's argument loses 5 or more Fatigue Levels, then the winner is clear.

entries.title: The Power of Truth
entries.summary: Optional modifiers to debate: starting fatigued when defending a patently flawed thesis, and a penalty from the Truthful Personality Trait when knowingly arguing a falsehood.
quotes: If a character knows that the side he is taking is false, then his Defense Totals are penalized by his Truthful Personality Trait, if any.

entries.title: Using Certamen Instead of Debate
entries.summary: Says when certamen can replace a formal debate at Tribunal and how to work out Argument Strength when a certamen settles only one issue in a larger case.
quotes: In this situation, simply use the actual Fatigue Levels lost rather than debating Fatigue Levels when calculating the Argument Strength of the winner.

entries.title: Other Uses for the Debate Rules
entries.summary: Applies the voting system to mundane courts and English juries, including how jurors are assigned and how The Gift affects a magus's Defense Total.
quotes: If a character with The Gift is on trial, only 10% of the jurors begin the case sympathetic towards that character's position.
Furthermore, the social penalty of The Gift is applied to the Defense Total of a magus when debating with mundanes before witnesses.

entries.title: Parish Schools
entries.summary: Describes how a character is accepted into a parish school with a social roll against a rural or urban Ease Factor, what the school costs and teaches, and how long a student typically stays.
quotes: Presence + Bargain or Charm or Guile + stress die vs. 6 (rural parish) or 9 (urban parish)
A student character studies two seasons out of the year from the parish priest.

entries.title: Cathedral Schools
entries.summary: Covers entry to a cathedral school (a social roll reduced by Bad Reputation), the cost of attending, how a character's Presence and Academic Reputation determine the number of students a cathedral teacher attracts, and the seasonal duties of a teacher.
quotes: Presence + Bargain, Charm, Guile or Intrigue + stress die – highest Bad Reputation vs. 12
A teacher can teach a number of students equal to five times the character's Teaching Ability
It costs a character one Mythic Pound to attend a cathedral school for one year.

entries.title: Monastic Schools
entries.summary: Monastic schools mostly admit their own brothers, use the cathedral school entry formula at a lower Ease Factor, and are of interest to magi chiefly for their libraries, which the precentor controls.
quotes: use the formula for gaining entrance to a cathedral school, but lower the Ease Factor to 9

entries.title: Urban Schools
entries.summary: Municipal schools admit citizens and foreigners using the cathedral school entry formula at different Ease Factors, and a master may teach as many students as his Teaching allows.
quotes: lower the Ease Factor to 9 if the prospective student is a citizen of the school's town. If he is a foreigner, make the Ease Factor 12.
(the teacher's Teaching score times five)

entries.title: Private Instructors
entries.summary: Explains the role of private instructors, the most common teachers at a Hermetic covenant, and how a character working as one owes his employer a share of each year.
quotes: The character will need to work for his employer for two seasons out of every year.

related.text: ArM5 p.72 Teachers bought with Build Points

entries.title: Acquiring a Teaching Position
entries.summary: An optional die-roll mechanic for finding academic work: a character spends a season and rolls against an Ease Factor set by the position, modified by Virtues and Academic Reputations. Failure wastes the season and a botch risks a wound or Bad Reputation.
quotes: Presence + appropriate Ability + Good Academic Reputation + bonus for Virtues – Bad Academic Reputation + stress die vs. Variable Ease Factor
If the roll fails, the season is wasted.

entries.title: Etiquette Performances
entries.summary: Introduces etiquette as symbolic communication at events and the three kinds of performance a character can attempt; an observer can tell which kind is being attempted with a roll.
quotes: an Intelligence + Etiquette roll against an Ease Factor of 3

entries.title: Individual Etiquette
entries.summary: Communication + Etiquette roll against a host-set Ease Factor to be the most memorable attendee at an event and earn Reputation experience; results can be given to another person.
quotes: A character wishing to make an individual impression at an event makes a Communication + Etiquette roll.
At minimum this is 6, but can be as high as 21.

entries.title: Competitive Etiquette (Etiquette Duels)
entries.summary: Etiquette duel in which each rival chooses a self-inflicted penalty to impose on both Communication + Etiquette rolls, then results are compared to see who looks boorish or wins the exchange.
quotes: A participant cannot choose a penalty greater than his Etiquette score.
The sum of both selected penalties is subtracted from the standard Etiquette roll of both individuals.

entries.title: Collaborative Etiquette
entries.summary: Group etiquette where participants' rolls are summed into a score compared with past events, with penalties for botches and sample scores for Tribunal feasts, Primus elections and symposia.
quotes: the rolls of all participants are added together
A person who botches during such an event reduces the score by 10, and may develop a poor Reputation.

entries.title: Money and Good Manners
entries.summary: Rules for boosting an Etiquette roll by spending money or by giving suitable gifts, and a roll to learn what gifts a particular magus would value.
quotes: The bonus is equal to +1 for each time the character spends the weekly income of all of his guests.
A character cannot gain a bonus higher than his Etiquette score by spending money.
An Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore + Reputation (of the receiver) roll against an Ease Factor of

entries.title: Intrigue and the Art of Indirect Action
entries.summary: Sidebar with an Intelligence + Intrigue roll table giving Ease Factors for learning about a noble target's enmities, vices and Flaws or for spreading and forging damaging information, plus the days and pounds each attempt costs.
quotes: For Ease Factors higher than 6, this takes (3 x Ease Factor) days and costs at least (Ease Factor / 3) pounds.

entries.title: Intrigue and the Art of Indirect Action
entries.summary: Graded Ease Factors for an Intelligence + Intrigue roll that uncover a noble's enmities, vices and secrets, or let the intriguer spread rumors or forged evidence to damage the target's Reputation. Time and cost scale with the Ease Factor, and targets or their friends may trace the culprit.
quotes: For Ease factors higher than 6, this takes (3 x Ease) days and costs at least (Ease / 3) pounds.
The following Ease Factors, for an Intelligence + Intrigue roll, demonstrate what a character might learn about potential allies, or the harm they may cause by spreading gossip.

entries.title: Using Intrigue to Aggregate Class Opinion
entries.summary: A stress roll with Intelligence + Intrigue lets a character gauge how an organization or the nobles of a region will react to an event, provided he knows the ruling class there.
quotes: A character may roll a stress die + Intelligence + Intrigue to feel the political mood of an organization, or the nobles of a region.

entries.title: Intrigue Rolls (Magi Trianomae)
entries.summary: It gives rolls and Ease Factors for influencing or interrogating an NPC with Intrigue, the Gift penalty, and the contested form between two active participants with a table of results by margin of victory.
quotes: Influence a non-player character: Presence + Intrigue vs. variable Ease Factor
Interrogate a non-player character: Communication + Intrigue vs. variable Ease Factor
the magus Trianomae rolls Presence + Intrigue + a stress die against the target's Communication + Intrigue + stress die

entries.title: Folk Ken and Guile
entries.summary: Guidance for secret Folk Ken rolls to read an important NPC, how Guile counters them, and how Folk Ken feeds a bonus or penalty to Intrigue rolls at a Tribunal.
quotes: the storyguide may make a secret Per + Folk Ken roll
A character attempting to deceive rolls Com + Guile.

entries.title: Money
entries.summary: The taxes vassals owe their liege: relief on inherited land (with the four graces that make it affordable) and discretionary aids paid on occasions such as knighting an heir or ransom.
quotes: it is capped at five pounds per manor, or 100 pounds for greater barons, regardless of actual income
In England, a lord owes approximately one year's income to his liege on the assumption of his title.

entries.title: Warriors
entries.summary: Military service owed by vassals: knights per manor, optional extra forces, peasant levies and what infantry are good for, and the limited number of days of service per year that vary by kingdom.
quotes: vassals are required to provide their lord with the service of one knight for per manor that their fief contained at the time it was originally granted
Assume that a powerful landowner must provide, at minimum, 20 knights when called to war.
In England this is 40 days, in Sicily 60.

entries.title: Scutage
entries.summary: The money a vassal may pay in place of sending knights to a war, why both sides like it, and the English rate and its history.
quotes: The scutage in England is usually two pounds per knight in 1220.

entries.title: Advice
entries.summary: A vassal's duty to attend his liege's court and give advice, and how a lord uses summonses to control vassals, build consensus, expose rebels and weigh competing interests.
quotes: A vassal asked to attend his liege's court has a duty to attend.

entries.title: Board Games
entries.summary: Describes period board games and the social value of playing them well, noting that Carouse may win a game but Etiquette is also needed to impress an opponent.
quotes: Playing well is a social grace, and while the Carouse Ability may allow a win, Etiquette is needed as well to impress one's opponent in what is, after all, a pursuit of polite company.

entries.title: Gambling
entries.summary: Notes common dice games and that Legerdemain or Luck can alter a die, and says which Abilities underlie gambling: Carouse for games of chance and Concentration for games of skill.
quotes: Games of chance are based upon the Ability Carouse, games of skill upon the Ability Concentration.

related.text: Tales of Mythic Europe: The Ship of Desire

entries.title: A Game of Chance?
entries.summary: Explains that imperfect dice let a skilled player gain an advantage with Perception + Carouse, with Luck and Legerdemain giving further edges and cheating leading to brawls.
quotes: use Perception + Carouse Ability to gain an advantage over an unskilled player

entries.title: Good Drink, Song, and Dance
entries.summary: Entertainment in noble halls and the dances of the period; knowing court dance steps uses Etiquette, local folk dances use Area Lore, and performing well depends on Athletics.
quotes: While knowledge of the steps of any given court dance is based upon Etiquette (local folk dances fall under Area Lore), a successful performance depends upon the Ability Athletics.

entries.title: Affinity
entries.summary: Defines a magnate's affinity and country as a political bloc, and says players can model it either as a Leadership bonus or by designing key members as agents.
quotes: Players may model the power their character has through affinity in two ways.

entries.title: Church Allies
entries.summary: What a powerful churchman brings as an ally, including military aid from Church manors, the effects and limits of excommunication and interdiction, and lending his Reputation to a cause.
quotes: A powerful churchman can lend his Reputation to a character's cause, so that disinterested or uninformed parties follow his guidance.

entries.title: Affinity Leadership
entries.summary: A bonus from a noble's Affinity score to social Ability rolls dealing with nobles, land-holding ecclesiastics and senior town councilors in his region, graded by rank and reduced when the area is split or the lord neglects his affinity. Examples of rolls it applies to are listed.
quotes: A character may use his Affinity score as a bonus to social Ability rolls that are directly related to his role as a powerful and respected person within a specific region.
The bonus above is halved (round down) if the area is divided between two warring affinities.
+5 For being the senior noble beneath the king in the region (count, earl, duke).

related.text: Chapter Three: A Comparison of Titles

entries.title: Short-Term Disguises
entries.summary: Rules for mundane disguises using the Guile Ability: an Intelligence + Guile roll made by the storyguide against a base Ease Factor, and an opposed Presence + Guile versus Intelligence + Folk Ken roll when interacting with someone.
quotes: To determine the success of a disguise, make an Intelligence + Guile roll, with a base Ease Factor of 9, modified according to the magnitude of the desired change, as laid out in the nearby insert.
Disguise Roll: Int + Guile + stress die vs. Ease Factor 9 + modifiers

entries.title: Deep Cover Disguises
entries.summary: Rules for long-term false identities: establishing a Reputation for the cover, how that Reputation reduces later Disguise rolls and grows with experience, the Virtue limits on roles, how it offsets the social penalty of The Gift, and how it fades when dormant.
quotes: This act grants a new Reputation as the disguised individual, at a score of 1 (see ArM5, page 167).
A character therefore subtracts his Reputation from the penalty to social rolls caused by The Gift, but only when dealing with those with whom he has regular contact.

entries.title: Disguise Roll Modifiers
entries.summary: A table of modifiers to the Disguise roll's Ease Factor for changes of social status, physical appearance or sex, and for how little preparation was possible.

entries.title: Disputatio
entries.summary: Introduces the formal academic debate: its three types (epideictic, deliberative, forensic), the roles of opponent, responder and judge, and how questions and exchanges are structured.
quotes: Disputationes have a set number of questions, determined beforehand and usually numbering seven, nine, or twelve.

entries.title: Basic Disputatio
entries.summary: Resolves a disputatio like a certamen: each disputer's argument has symbolic Fatigue Levels worn down by Attack, Defense, Weakening and Resistance Totals, followed by an Over-Exertion check for real fatigue. Several Virtues and Flaws modify these totals.
quotes: Attack Total: Communication + Ability + stress die
Weakening Total: Intelligence + Attack Advantage
Disputatio Over-Exertion Check: Stamina + stress die vs. Ease Factor equal to the number of rounds of the disputatio

entries.title: Advanced Disputatio
entries.summary: Optional additions to the disputatio rules: minimum Ease Factors for statements, questions from the crowd, public Advent and Lent disputes, resolving a private examination as a disputatio, and experience rewards for winning.
quotes: Roll a stress die (no botch) to determine the Attack Total.
Disputatio experience point rewards should not be granted more than once a season.

entries.title: The Feast
entries.summary: Introduces the noble feast as a frequent and special event, and notes that a host who fails to put on a feast for a guest earns a Reputation for being inhospitable.
quotes: a host who does not put on a feast for a guest will soon gain a Reputation for being inhospitable

entries.title: Seating the Guests, and Good Manners
entries.summary: How a hall is laid out and guests are seated by precedence, with Etiquette used to place guests correctly, and the contrast between Etiquette at the high table and Carouse at the lower tables.
quotes: Placing someone in too low a position can be seen as an insult, so Etiquette is used to decide the correct seating.

entries.title: The Host
entries.summary: How the quality of hospitality affects a host, including the insult of poor hospitality, the use by kings of demanded hospitality to weaken vassals, and the Reputation (or even a Gratitude point) earned by an exceptional feast.
quotes: a good host who puts on a lavish feast will soon gain a Reputation for hospitality and generosity, and for feasts that are exceptional in food, entertainment, and gifts, even a Gratitude point

entries.title: Peasant Loyalty
entries.summary: Peasants are not loyal to strangers, lowering taxes does not simply buy loyalty, and the loyalty of a noble's military household may be tracked with the Covenants loyalty system.
quotes: Peasants in Mythic Europe are not required to be loyal to their lord.
The loyalty of the mesnie may be tracked using the system given in Covenants, page 38

entries.title: Community Loyalty
entries.summary: Magi can keep rich peasants from becoming restive by offering a better deal than a royal charter gives, earning loyalty to the community rather than to the magi themselves.
quotes: Magi can prevent their rich peasants from becoming restive by offering them a deal better than that provided by the nearest town's royal charter.

entries.title: Flight and Rebellion
entries.summary: Explains why the Covenants loyalty mechanic fits large households but not noble-peasant relations, and what drives peasants to flee, rebel, or collectively refuse to work.
quotes: The loyalty mechanic given in Covenants, beginning on page 36
A peasant flees the land when it seems he has better prospects elsewhere.

entries.title: Academic Reputations
entries.summary: Academic Reputations are Reputations that grow like an Ability from experience points earned only through scholarly deeds, with lists of deeds that raise a Good or Bad Academic Reputation. Hermetic study gives no Academic Reputation.
quotes: Each time a character does any of the following, he gains one Academic Reputation experience point:
Stagnating gains a character 1 experience point per year.
Studying, increasing, or writing about the Hermetic Arts does not award Academic Reputation experience points

entries.title: Gaining and Losing Reputation
entries.summary: Lists tourney achievements and the experience points each earns towards Prudhomme Reputation in a season, taking the highest reward earned.
quotes: Extracting ransom from a stronger opponent earns 2 experience points.

entries.title: Family Reputation
entries.summary: Families carry shared Reputations that characters may use instead of their own among strangers, shaped by every family member's actions.
quotes: characters may use this Reputation instead of their own, among people who do not personally know the character

entries.title: Horror stories for grogs
entries.summary: Advice for running horror, which leans on Personality Traits such as Brave and can represent madness as temporarily imposed high Personality Traits that govern reactions to certain stimuli.
quotes: Horror stories make extensive use of Personality Traits (particularly the Brave Trait)

entries.title: Rewards for grog stories
entries.summary: Grogs earn experience like other characters but seldom gain vis or items, so the storyguide can reward success with experience in a Reputation among the covenfolk, favors, mentoring, an agency, or personalized equipment.
quotes: Grogs earn experience points at the same rate as any other character

entries.title: Representatives
entries.summary: Grogs often speak for magi because of The Gift; this section covers how bribes work, rough wages for context, and how a bribe of a day's or a week's pay gives a Minor or Major equipment bonus.
quotes: A bribe equivalent to a day's pay grants a Minor equipment bonus (see earlier), whereas a bribe equivalent to a week's pay grants a Major equipment bonus.

entries.title: Gaining Information
entries.summary: Getting locals to talk uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll, with the Ease Factor raised by the local's Suspicious Personality Trait.
quotes: An average Communication + Folk Ken roll is usually sufficient to get an individual to talk, but increase the Ease Factor by the local's Suspicious Personality Trait.

entries.title: Craft Guilds
entries.summary: Describes how craft guilds are organised around a Craft Ability, which towns have them, which appear first, and how guilds split into narrower specialisations in later periods.
quotes: For sagas starting in 1220, guilds generally correspond directly to a particular Craft Ability

entries.title: Number of Guilds in a Town
entries.summary: A rough table of how many guilds a town has by population size and by saga date.
quotes: 1,000 or less | 0–1

entries.title: Overwork (Reputation Penalties)
entries.summary: Working extra seasons or living below one's means to gain Labor Points faster earns a negative Reputation for impiety or miserliness.
quotes: A character who is not Poor, but works three or more seasons in a year, gains a negative Reputation.
This imposes 1 or 3 experience in a Reputation for miserliness every year.

entries.title: Labor Points (sidebar)
entries.summary: Defines Labor Points as a measure of a worker's day-to-day output in seasons spent earning Exposure, how many are needed per year to keep a business or crop going, and how a foreman can pool workers' points.
quotes: An individual must accumulate 36 Labor Points in a year to maintain his business or grow his crops.
he accumulates a number of Labor Points equal to three times his Communication + Profession Ability, or his Dexterity + Craft Ability

entries.title: Marriage and Dowries
entries.summary: How noble marriages are arranged, what the Church requires, and how dowries and widows' portions are handled in Italy, France and England, with a game-ready rule of thumb for a widow's share.
quotes: For game purposes, assume this is one third of his estate, and that she likely loses this property if she remarries.

entries.title: Size of Dowries
entries.summary: A checklist of circumstances that push a bride's dowry down, with the note that dowries are more generous when those statements are untrue and that an exceptional bride may even earn her family a dower.
quotes: Conversely, dowries are more generous if any of these statements are untrue.

entries.title: Medieval Money
entries.summary: Explains coins versus moneys-of-account and the fixed relationship between pound, shilling, penny and mark in the West, and how eastern bezants and denars relate to them.
quotes: In the West, a Mythic Pound equals 20 Mythic Shillings and 240 Mythic Pennies.
In the East, a Mythic Pound equals two Mythic Bezants or Denars.

entries.title: Price List (common goods and quality multipliers)
entries.summary: Sample prices for everyday goods for story flavor, extrapolated by the troupe for unlisted items, plus quality multipliers applied to a price from shoddy to wondrous; not intended for working out merchants' or craftsmen's yearly income.
quotes: Adjust the price of an item by its quality.

entries.title: The Gratitude System
entries.summary: An optional structured advancement system in which characters earn Gratitude points from their lord for service beyond their station, then redeem them for higher office, land or goods. The text lists how many points different kinds of story outcome are worth.
quotes: Characters earn Gratitude points when they perform a service to their lord that is beyond that required by their station.
If the story requires the character to complete a feat that will be widely renowned for its difficulty

entries.title: Advancement Requirements Table
entries.summary: A table of what a character needs, and what it costs the granting lord, to move between ranks such as serf, freeman, knight, bacheler, landed noble, banneret and baron, or to take an office. Notes explain how many heroic or exceptional services a promotion normally takes.
quotes: Gratitude 10, marriage to suitable heiress, or claiming land during war, or being offered land that has returned to the lord.
Appointment as an officer to Greater Baron or higher requires Gratitude 10, Landed Noble (at minimum), Reputation for loyalty to the lord, vacancy in the office, and office-specific traits.

related.text: Chapter Three: A Comparison of Titles

entries.title: Preaching
entries.summary: Preaching is a Profession Ability used to sway an audience to a course of action with a Communication roll against an Ease Factor, and to teach Theology to regular listeners over a season. Covers audience size, language requirement, and failure and botch results.
quotes: Communication + Preaching + stress die vs. 12
The group can be no larger than the character's Leadership score times ten.

entries.title: Preaching
entries.summary: Rules guidance for popular preaching: preachers are handled as performers with the Profession: Preacher Ability and Reputation, may change listeners' Personality Traits or teach Lores, and can be a study source for listeners. Lay preachers and the unordained risk trouble if they stray into doctrine.
quotes: Reputation is everything, and preachers are perhaps best treated as performers using the Art & Academe rules
If a character dedicates a season of free time to following a preacher, the study source is equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the preacher's performance in the relevant Ability.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Care of Souls

entries.title: All-Grog Sagas
entries.summary: Introduces sagas in which players run only grogs while magi are storyguide characters, and suggests running a grog saga in parallel with a standard saga, possibly with an alternative storyguide.
quotes: One saga deals with the actions of the magi, the other the consequences that those actions have on the turb

entries.title: A Noble Saga
entries.summary: Describes a saga built on a noble household where the lord and a few select staff are companions and everyone else, including his sons of age, are grogs because they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.
quotes: Even the baron's sons who have reached their majority could be considered grog characters, since they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.

entries.title: Gifted Babies
entries.summary: Describes how the social penalties of The Gift affect an infant's relationships, from loving parents to abandonment, as background for a Gifted child character.
quotes: The negative social influence of The Gift permeates every relationship in life, both intimate and incidental.

entries.title: The Gift Revealed
entries.summary: Explains that The Gift can show itself at birth, at puberty or after a trauma, and that its social consequences begin as soon as it emerges.
quotes: Sometimes it is evident at birth, other times it is triggered by puberty or an early traumatic event.

entries.title: Purchasing Supplies for Travel
entries.summary: Where and when grogs can buy food while traveling, with example prices and a rule of thumb for what it costs to feed a grog for a day.
quotes: Broadly speaking, it costs a Mythic Penny to feed a grog for a day, if you are buying rather than growing his food.

entries.title: Arranging Accommodation
entries.summary: Finding lodging in remote places uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll against an Ease Factor set by the kind of accommodation, with The Gift's social penalty applying if the peasants have talked with the magi.
quotes: make a Communication + Folk Ken roll, using the Ease Factors in the following table

entries.title: Examinations
entries.summary: A student faces a single, difficult private examination per career stage and then a ceremonial public examination that cannot be failed, with the candidate paying for the ceremony.
quotes: University students take only one exam per stage of their academic careers.
He cannot fail his public examination

entries.title: Passing Examinations
entries.summary: An abstract way to resolve a private examination: after the required years of study and a minimum Good Academic Reputation, the candidate makes an Exam Total against an Ease Factor set by the license. Passing the public examination only depends on paying for it.
quotes: Communication + Artes Liberales + Good Academic Reputation - Bad Academic Reputation + Stress Die vs. 6
A baccalaureate candidate needs a Good Academic Reputation of at least 1, a magister in artibus candidate 2, and a doctoral candidate needs a minimum score of 3.

entries.title: Wardship of Heirs
entries.summary: How a liege takes wardship of a dead vassal's heirs and heiresses: fostering, control of the revenues, choice of marriage partners, disparagement, and the value of heirs and heiresses as rewards.
quotes: going straight into the treasury of the liege until the child turns 21 if male, or marries if female

entries.title: Wardship of Widows
entries.summary: How a widow may become the ward of her husband's lord, what portion of the estate she is entitled to, and how the Church views the trade in marriages.
quotes: A widow is entitled to a portion of her husband's estate, fixed at the time of marriage, to maintain herself until her death.

entries.title: Income Bands (Trivial to Legendary)
entries.summary: Defines the six bands of annual profit (Trivial, Minor, Lesser, Typical, Greater, Legendary), what each means as spending money after expenses, example enterprises, and which Social Status Virtues buy each band.
quotes: The income figure listed below for each band is the amount of money a character in that band could spend frivolously in a year without damaging his source of income.
A single workshop, in an average craft, earns 10 Mythic Pounds for its owner each year.

entries.title: Money and Investment (Labor Points to Pounds)
entries.summary: Explains that Labor Points cannot be directly converted to money, and gives a guideline table of what a block of Labor Points is worth in pounds for each income band.
quotes: the average character earns around 6 Labor Points a season, multiplied according to his level of wealth
This means that 9 Labor Points are worth:

entries.title: Double Agents and Hostile Takeovers
entries.summary: Extends the Appendix agent rules: recruiting a rival's agent as a double or triple agent, and taking over a whole agency by impersonating its principal to use the Bond Strength he has built.
quotes: as soon as the Resistance of the agent reaches zero, he becomes a double agent, working for both agencies, but most loyal to the principal with the highest Bond Strength.

entries.title: Sponsors: Patrons and Benefactors
entries.summary: Every artwork needs a sponsor, either a benefactor for one piece or a patron for ongoing support. The artist spends a season rolling to find one, with modifiers by sponsor type and standing, increasingly wealthy sponsors required as Reputation grows, a ways to lose a sponsor, and a minimum payment when a player character sponsors an artist.
quotes: Finding a Sponsor: Communication + Bargain + Artist Reputation + stress die vs. 12 + modifiers
A player can make a Perception + Folk Ken + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12.
Cost to Sponsor an Artwork (Completed in One Season): At least 1 Mythic Pound per point of Artist Reputation

entries.title: Negotiation (Bargain)
entries.summary: Procedure for haggling over a price: appraise the goods' value, make opposed Bargain rolls for buyer and seller, derive the lowest final price from the difference, and optionally roll to read the seller's willingness.
quotes: The buyer can attempt to determine the value by making a Perception + Bargain roll, with an Ease Factor of 9.
Communication + Bargain + simple die for the buyer and seller
Regardless of how good the buyer's Bargain roll is, the sale price is never less than half of the initial value.

entries.title: The Benefice
entries.summary: Explains the benefice as the income attached to a parish, who may assign it, the legitimate reasons for a priest to be absent (study, service elsewhere, pluralism), and how licenses of absence and benefice exchanges are handled.

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Election of the Bishop
entries.summary: How a bishop is elected by the cathedral canons, what candidate qualifications mean in game terms (Latin literacy and usually a positive Church reputation), and the grounds on which an election can be challenged by petition.
quotes: The bishop is elected by a simple majority, in a secret ballot, of the cathedral canons.

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: The Commanding Aura
entries.summary: Divinely appointed rulers and religious leaders gain Magic Resistance, a Soak bonus and an authority aura, with scores by rank and faith, and how relics and sanctions interact.
quotes: They receive a Magic Resistance score with the value listed below and a bonus to their Soak equal to their Magic Resistance score divided by 5.
In the Latin Christian world, the supreme religious leader is the Pope, with a Magic Resistance of 25.

entries.title: Is Love True?
entries.summary: Guidance for the troupe on whether and how courtly love features in the saga, with three rules of thumb for romance subplots.
quotes: no character with the True Love or Lost Love Virtue or Flaw may ever be caught up in romance, except with the object of their affections.

entries.title: Criminals
entries.summary: Abstract rules for nobles hiring criminals: Intrigue is used to hire them, their results can be resolved without playing a scene, and typical prices are given for assassination, beatings, bribes, kidnapping, sabotage, spying and treachery. A table gives the added difficulty for different kinds of sabotage.
quotes: the hiring character rolls Communication + Intrigue and uses the result in place of the proxy's roll, to determine the degree of success
Sabotage requires a Dexterity + Stealth + stress roll that exceeds the Perception + Awareness + stress roll of the most skilled sentry guarding the facility that the agent seeks to harm.

entries.title: Taking the Cross
entries.summary: Rules for a character committing to a Church-preached crusade: he gains an indulgence for outstanding penance and a temporary Faith Point, must fund his own travel and upkeep, and may at the troupe's discretion shed a Social Status Flaw.
quotes: He receives a single temporary Faith Point for the commitment

entries.title: Family and Inheritance
entries.summary: How a magus's birth or adoptive family interacts with the Gift and with law: choosing apprentices, and why magi cannot hold feudal land but may inherit other property and have stewards for child heirs.
quotes: Magi may not enter into feudal relationships, and so may not inherit land.

entries.title: Holy Influence
entries.summary: How holy characters with spiritual authority inspire temporary Personality Traits in followers, by personal influence over a season or by a short ceremony, with a roll that sets the strength of the trait.
quotes: HOLY INFLUENCE: simple die + Presence + Leadership

entries.title: Setting Up Business (physician income)
entries.summary: Physicians and chirurgeons earn money using Medicine or Chirurgy in place of a Craft or Profession, with income brackets by training and location, and licensing restrictions in some cities.
quotes: Physicians use (Intelligence + Medicine) to calculate Craft totals and labor points, whereas chirurgeons use (Dexterity + Chirurgy).

related.text: City & Guild (earning income through Craft or Profession)

entries.title: Inheritance
entries.summary: Describes how land passes to sons, nominated heirs, appanages or daughters in different parts of Mythic Europe, and the measures nobles use to limit fratricide.
quotes: The average noble family fails to provide a male heir every fourth generation, so this churning of lands is common.

entries.title: Translation
entries.summary: Rules for communicating across languages: rolls needed at low Language scores, how fluency limits use of social Abilities, and penalties to both speakers for dialect differences and related languages.
quotes: A character with a Language Ability of 2 or less needs to make Communication + Language rolls to get his point across
Unless she is fluent (Language Ability 5 or better), use of a character's social Abilities is limited by her Language score.

entries.title: Trading Companies (capo, partners, factors)
entries.summary: How a trading company is structured around a capo, partners and distant factors, how traders may work for a company, and how Employed by a Company interacts with Poor and Wealthy.
quotes: A character may have both the Employed by a Company and Poor Flaws, but this requires an explanation approved by the troupe

entries.title: Military
entries.summary: Covers the household knights (the mesnie) of a lord, the status of a bacheler and a carissimus, and how mesnie loyalty works in practice. Includes Intelligence + Intrigue rolls to recall a mesnie's common features or find a lord who favors a skill.
quotes: A character may make an Intelligence + Intrigue roll against an Ease Factor of 6 to recall if the mesnie members of a lord with whom he is interacting have a common feature.
A knight becomes a bacheler by being offered a place in a mesnie.

entries.title: Retinue
entries.summary: Explains the four parts of a magnate's household (family, military, clerical and menial) and gives typical household sizes by noble rank, useful for sizing a lord's following.
quotes: Speaking loosely, the household of a lord of the manor averages 10, that of a landed knight 16, that of a banneret 24, that of a baron 40, and that of an earl 140.

entries.title: Patronage
entries.summary: How giving gifts, grants and support to a specific social group earns a Reputation with that group, a Loyal Trait in the recipient and sometimes Gratitude, with notes on each kind of patron-recipient group.
quotes: improves a Loyal Personality Trait in the recipient that is directed toward the patron
Reputations can pertain to Local (meaning all in the vicinity), Clergy, Order of Hermes, Nobles, or Academics.

entries.title: Serf or Villein
entries.summary: Legal status of serfs and what they owe their lord in rent, week works and boon works, the censum to buy off week work, and how tradesmen differ from other villeins.
quotes: Serfs owe their lord rent, week works, and boon works.
Rent is traditionally a penny an acre a year, but may be far higher.

entries.title: A Random Method of Life
entries.summary: Companion method for a character waiting to inherit: check each person ahead of them for a new legitimate child, then check each child for a random age of death.
quotes: Then roll a die for each, assuming that on average half of them do have a child.

entries.title: The Cost of Breaking Convention
entries.summary: Optional guideline that penalizes a magus who dresses above his station, trails armed men, or flaunts his familiar in public when dealing with mundanes, unless he makes an effort to follow convention.
quotes: he suffers an additional –1 social interaction penalty

entries.title: Growing Used to The Gifted
entries.summary: People can grow used to a Gifted individual over time, so grogs use the covenant's Prevailing Loyalty rather than the magus's Gift penalty for Loyal rolls, with an optional system of separate Loyalty scores per magus.
quotes: An individual grog begins with a Loyal Personality Trait that is up to 3 points different from the turb's Prevailing Loyalty.

entries.title: Warring Faiths
entries.summary: A character can write books or debate against another faith by combining two Theology Abilities, and gains extra Academic Reputation experience from such a challenge.
quotes: the character must average the scores in the two Theology Abilities to determine the maximum level of the summa
he receives double the normal amount of Academic Reputation experience points

entries.title: Paying Tithes Inadequately
entries.summary: What is owed in tithes, the common ways peasants shortchange the Church, exemptions for the very poor, and how strictly tithes are enforced.
quotes: One tenth of everything that a person gets must be given to the Church.

entries.title: Court Decisions (Quick Trial Roll)
entries.summary: A quick method to decide a trial: a social roll of Communication plus the relevant law Ability against an Ease Factor adjusted by the defendant's guilt, reputation and witnesses.
quotes: make a Communication + Civil and Canon Law roll against an Ease Factor of 6, on behalf of the defendant or his proxy
Defendant actually is innocent | –3

entries.title: False Scholars
entries.summary: A character can pose as a student to gain a university education without paying, rolling each season to avoid being discovered; success gives full experience, failure half, and a botch brings legal trouble.
quotes: Communication + Guile + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9
Penalties from The Gift apply to this roll.

entries.title: Merchants and Bankers (Vis Exchange, Loans, Liens, Pawning)
entries.summary: How Redcaps trade vis between Technique and Form types at fixed exchange rates, and lend, pawn, take liens and speculate on vis and magic items, including interest rates, loan limits, vis accounts, notary letters and Tribunal treasuries.
quotes: Generally, they trade one unit of vis for two.
Fair practice is to both pay and charge 20% interest annually
ten pounds of silver might be considered roughly equivalent to a pawn of vis

entries.title: The Urban Merchant
entries.summary: Describes the urban merchant, the least affluent trader type, who retails in one city, and what such a character offers a covenant.
quotes: They should select the Merchant Social Status Virtue.

entries.title: Urban Merchant Scale of Affluence
entries.summary: Describes poor, average and wealthy urban merchants by lifestyle, home and trade.
quotes: Wealthy merchants own their own home, and trade from a store near the market that they might own.

entries.title: Marriage and Dowries
entries.summary: How marriage consent and dowries work for merchants, including a husband's rights over a dowry in Italy, France and England and the share of an estate a widow keeps for game purposes.
quotes: For game purposes, assume this is one third of his estate, and that she likely loses this property if she remarries.

entries.title: Calculating Dowries for Merchants' Daughters
entries.summary: Sidebar procedure for working out a bride's dowry from her father's annual profit and Social Status relative to the groom, with factors that make a dowry larger or smaller.
quotes: This is figured by multiplying the father's annual profit by 10, then dividing by the number of children he has, except any daughters already married.

entries.title: The Local Carrier
entries.summary: Describes local carriers, who work one route with stable goods, the waterman variant, and how they serve covenants.
quotes: All local traders have the Merchant Virtue.

entries.title: Local Carrier Scale of Abundance
entries.summary: Describes the cargo, home and staff of poor, average and wealthy local carriers.
quotes: A local carrier of average wealth carries enough cargo to fill a single four-wheeled cart.

entries.title: The Merchant Adventurer
entries.summary: Describes the merchant adventurer who commands a ship or caravan, how the crew is built from the travel chapter's notes, and the city's expectations in time of war.
quotes: All merchant adventurers, regardless of wealth or poverty, are in command of a ship, or a caravan of wagons or pack beasts.

entries.title: Ventures (planning a trading voyage)
entries.summary: Factors a merchant weighs when planning a venture with no certain buyer: return cargo, languages of trade, bulk versus luxury goods, and crew size traded against cargo space.
quotes: Extra crew take up cargo space at the rate of one ton per eight additional sailors.

related.text: City & Guild Chapter 5: Travel, Ship Combat

entries.title: The Factor
entries.summary: Describes the factor who manages a trading house's assets in one city, his role and the Abilities factors typically have.
quotes: Factors are skilled in Bargain, Civil or Common Law, Folk Ken, Leadership, and Profession Trader.

entries.title: Factor Scale of Affluence
entries.summary: Describes the lifestyle of poor, average and wealthy factors, company versus independent, and the consequences of failing to keep up appearances.
quotes: The Factor Virtue is also used for independent traders who have sufficient capital to organize multiple shipments

entries.title: The Capo
entries.summary: Describes the capo who leads a merchant company, sets its strategy and culture, and what a capo offers a covenant.
quotes: All characters with this role must select the Capo Social Status Virtue.

entries.title: Capo Scale of Affluence
entries.summary: Describes poor, average and wealthy capos and the role of the capo's house as the company's central office.
quotes: An average capo lives luxuriously, like a nobleman.

entries.title: Legal Action (investment of time)
entries.summary: Besides the story, a merchant may bring a lawsuit as an investment of time, resolved by opposed Intelligence + Law rolls with modifiers for true or false claims and a change to a Reputation on a win.
quotes: The merchant compares the Intelligence + Civil or Canon Law roll of his representative with that of his opponent

entries.title: Convoys and Caravans
entries.summary: Leading a convoy earns Reputation and Labor Points as a story or as an investment of time, and a failed convoy damages Reputation.
quotes: half a season's worth of Labor Points per season as an investment of time

entries.title: Finding Investors
entries.summary: A merchant adventurer needs a backer for each venture until his Reputation is high enough, and a season spent winning a sponsor earns Labor Points as a story or investment.
quotes: until the merchant has a positive Reputation of at least 3

entries.title: Warfare and Blockades (blockade running)
entries.summary: How war reroutes trade, and the seasonal shiphandling roll a blockade-runner makes against an Ease Factor to slip past the besiegers.
quotes: Blockade running requires a seasonal shiphandling roll (Dexterity + suitable Profession) against an Ease Factor of 15

entries.title: Change of Government (investment of time)
entries.summary: A factor can win over a new ruler as a story, or as an investment of time that yields Labor Points from Communication and Intrigue and the Favor of a minor political figure.
quotes: (Communication + Intrigue) x Wealth multiplier Labor Points

entries.title: Young Talent (investment of time)
entries.summary: Recruiting young merchants into the house earns Labor Points as a story, or as an investment of time by rolling Communication + Leadership times the Wealth Multiplier, plus Favors owed by the recruits.
quotes: As an investment of time, roll [{Communication + Leadership} x Wealth Multiplier] and gain that number of Labor Points

entries.title: Personal Pleasure and Aggrandizement (entertaining guests)
entries.summary: A capo may throw a lavish themed party as an investment of time, rolling a die plus Characteristic plus the theme Ability with bonus from money spent, and gains Favors from the result; also notes local etiquette on display and marriage.
quotes: A capo may entertain guests as an investment of time, throwing a lavish party, lasting days, that emphasizes a particular Ability.
The character gains the benefits of one Favor Flaw for every five points of this total, rounding up.

entries.title: Skullduggery (hiring criminals with Intrigue)
entries.summary: Characters committing commercial crime through hired professionals roll Communication + Intrigue in place of the proxy's roll when the crime is not played out as a story.
quotes: the hiring character rolls Communication + Intrigue and uses the result in place of the proxy's roll

entries.title: Assassination, Beatings and Kidnapping (costs)
entries.summary: Typical prices for hired assassins, beatings and kidnappings, and the Reputation cost of habitually having poor people attacked.
quotes: An assassin usually charges two pounds for this service.

entries.title: Bribes
entries.summary: Bribe sizes scale with the official's wage and the risk of the favor, from a week's to a year's wages, with recurring favors paid as a percentage.
quotes: An easily granted favor costs a week's wages.

entries.title: Sabotage
entries.summary: Hired agents attempt sabotage with a Dexterity + Stealth roll against the best sentry's Perception + Awareness roll, with a bonus for each extra sentry and for the type of sabotage.
quotes: Sabotage requires a Dexterity + Stealth + stress roll that exceeds the Perception + Awareness + stress roll of the most skilled sentry guarding the facility that the agent seeks to harm.

entries.title: Sabotage Table
entries.summary: Table of the sentry's Awareness bonus by type of sabotage, from defacement to spoilage, with examples.

entries.title: Spying
entries.summary: Factors keep spies, often at little cost, but spies asked to betray their own business demand very large payments.
quotes: Spies require very large payments for their assistance, sometimes as much as they earn by their legitimate profession.

entries.title: Theft
entries.summary: Large-scale theft between rival houses needs at least a brief story, and the thieves usually demand a share of the stolen cargo's value.
quotes: The thieves working for the characters usually request at least half the value of the stolen cargo for their effort, in coin.

entries.title: The Unemployed and Day Workers
entries.summary: The jobless and day-laboring poor outside the planting and reaping seasons, and the rule in some regions that a stranger who stays on a manor long enough becomes the lord's villein.
quotes: the unemployment rate is around twenty percent outside of the planting and reaping seasons.
In France, any stranger who dwells in a manor for more than a year is automatically the villein of the lord

entries.title: Famuli and Other Retained Servants
entries.summary: The lord's retained household servants, how they are housed and fed, and how their status compares with villeins who farm their own land.
quotes: The famuli are the household staff of the lord.

entries.title: Offices for Villeins
entries.summary: How the reeve, beadle, hayward and other village offices are filled, what each does, how they are paid, and why reeves are disliked and corrupt.
quotes: Reeves are usually paid a small wage: generally double whatever is being paid to other laborers
This fee is as high as a shilling a head a year in some places.

entries.title: Free Peasants
entries.summary: What freedom means for a peasant, the service free men may still owe, how freedom passes by birth and marriage, and where free peasants are most common.
quotes: Free peasants make up less than ten percent of the population of most manors

entries.title: Officers
entries.summary: The steward and the bailiff who run a manor for the lord, their duties, accounting obligations, and typical pay by size of holding.
quotes: The steward, or seneschal, is the lord's representative on the manor.
A bailiff is paid approximately ten shillings a year in the smallest fiefs

entries.title: Guild Members (Ranks, Roster and Required Abilities)
entries.summary: Introduces guild ranks, the guild roster, and the Abilities guild members need, including minimum Guild Lore scores by rank.
