quotes: Journeymen need at least a Guild Lore score of 1, masters need a 2, and senior masters and deans must have a Guild Lore score of 3.

entries.title: Guild Officials and Inquisitors
entries.requires: Virtue: Senior Master (to play an official)
entries.summary: Describes the board of guild officials, how they are chosen, their terms, powers (including defrocking masters), and the inquisitors who inspect workshops; playing an official needs no extra mechanic beyond the Virtue.
quotes: Guild officials retain their office for six months, at which point they return to the pool of senior master candidates.
Substandard goods are confiscated on the spot, with a fine equal to the goods' value imposed on the master.

entries.title: Craftswomen and the Male Guild Sponsor
entries.requires: Female guild character (Virtue: Male Guild Sponsor)
entries.summary: Explains how women are restricted in guilds and the ways they enter them through a father's or husband's name on the roster, and how the Male Guild Sponsor Virtue lets a female character join any guild in a saga.
quotes: allows female characters to participate in any guild of the player's choice
Even if a woman gains the status of a master, she is legally forbidden the opportunity to be a guild official.

entries.title: Service Guilds
entries.summary: Service guilds follow the craft guild rules, with Profession replacing Craft for ability requirements and labor pools replacing workshops.
quotes: Replace the requirement for specific scores in a Craft Ability with a requirement for the same score in a Profession Ability.

entries.title: Cluniac Influence on Petitioning the Church
entries.requires: Favor of a Cluniac prior or abbot
entries.summary: Cluniac abbots and priors carry extra weight with the Church hierarchy, giving a bonus to Petitioning the Church totals when their favor is won.
quotes: Gaining the favor of a Cluniac prior or abbot gives a +1 bonus to totals for Petitioning the Church (see Chapter 3: The Diocese) over and above the usual bonuses.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Cistercian Influence on Petitioning the Church
entries.summary: The Cistercians' standing with the papacy gives a bonus to Petitioning the Church totals when a Cistercian abbot's favor is gained.
quotes: gaining the favor of a Cistercian abbot gives a +3 bonus to totals for Petitioning the Church (See Chapter 3: The Diocese) over and above the usual bonuses.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Vallumbrosan Papal Influence
entries.requires: Support of a Vallumbrosan abbot; petition addressed to the papacy or curia
entries.summary: Vallumbrosan influence over the papacy adds a large bonus to the total of a petition made to the pope or curia, on top of the normal bonus for an abbot's support.
quotes: If the papacy or curia are the recipients of a petition, add +5 to the total in addition to the normal bonus for the support of an abbot.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Templar Chaplains and Petitioning
entries.summary: Templar clergy petition their own commanders, the grand master or the pope rather than bishops, and may act on their own authority up to a set Ease Factor for matters within the order.
quotes: Brother-priests may, without reference to any outside authority, perform any action with an Ease Factor of 18 or less

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Costs
entries.summary: What a patron spends to host a tournament, the quality of prizes, and a rule of thumb for how much he should spend relative to his Prudhomme Reputation.
quotes: a patron should spend ten Mythic Pounds per point of his Prudhomme Reputation to hold a tournament.

related.text: City & Guild p.69 superior quality works

entries.title: Team Sponsors
entries.summary: The cost to a sponsor of retaining knights to fight under his banner at tournaments.
quotes: Most nobles can expect to pay four Mythic Pounds per season per knight retained for tourney.

entries.title: Awards
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on how prizes are won at a tournament and how valuable a prize should be.
quotes: Storyguides should consider one Mythic Pound per point of Prudhomme Reputation as a baseline.

entries.title: Buying Toys (faerie market prices)
entries.requires: Access to the Devil's Lane market
entries.summary: How faerie merchants price premade toys in vis, the negotiating gap between the opening offer and the bottom line, and how payment is disguised as unusual goods containing vis.
quotes: The faerie merchants sell toys for the number of pawns of vis required to create it plus one pawn.
Charged items cost a minimum of one pawn of vis per charge.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie pp.18-19 Vis sources

entries.title: Commissioning Toys
entries.requires: Access to the Devil's Lane market
entries.summary: Price rules for commissioning a custom toy from the faeries, including the required Art type and upfront payment.
quotes: the bottom-line price is twice the vis cost
The initial price is four times the vis cost.

entries.title: Manumission by Lay Lords
entries.requires: Serf character or covenfolk seeking freedom
entries.summary: How a lay lord frees a serf, what influences the price, and rule-of-thumb costs for a player character to buy freedom or to enter schooling for the priesthood.
quotes: As a rule of thumb, a player character can purchase freedom, for himself and his descendants, for between six and ten pounds.
For player characters, assume this sum to be ten shillings

entries.title: Manumission by Membership of a Town's Guild
entries.summary: A villein becomes free through town guild membership, not just by living in a town for a year and a day; this usually needs a wealthy patron.
quotes: To become free the person must not stray from the town, and must be accepted as a resident by the authorities of the town.

entries.title: House Reputation (advocates and largesse)
entries.summary: A merchant house has Reputations that its representatives borrow and change; they can be improved by representatives' deeds, hired advocates (limited to a small modifier) and largesse such as festivals and public buildings, with a cap on advocates per person.
quotes: Several advocates working together can warp a victim's perception of the house markedly, but cannot ever produce a Reputation modifier greater than 3.
No person may be influenced by more than three advocates, altering the same Reputation, at the same time.

entries.title: Largesse: The Costs of Excellent Building (table)
entries.summary: Table of the cost in pounds of public works such as monuments, roads, wells, bridges, mills, chapels and churches that a house may sponsor to improve its Reputation.

entries.title: Company Reputations
entries.summary: Deeds done under a company banner build a Reputation for the company itself, usable only by knights who ride in its colors.
quotes: Companies have a Reputation named after its leader or chant, which applies only within the tournament circuit.

entries.title: Patronage
entries.summary: Experience points toward Prudhomme Reputation earned by hosting tournaments and by commissioning an artist to record them, shared among co-hosts.
quotes: Hosting one or more tournaments in a season earns 1 experience point, or 2 if the event is particularly lavish.

entries.title: Templar Banking, Letters of Credit and Insurance
entries.summary: How the Templars handle deposits, letters of credit that can be redeemed at a distant priory, administration of pilgrims' assets, and a form of physical and spiritual insurance.
quotes: In exchange, they receive a letter from that priory stating the value of the deposit.

entries.title: Trial by Ordeal
entries.summary: Lists the types of judicial ordeal in Mythic Europe and notes a Just temper may arise around trials, favoring the innocent.
quotes: Their confidence could bring about a Just temper before the trial

entries.title: Player Characters and the Commanding Aura
entries.requires: Rank in an ecclesiastical or secular hierarchy
entries.summary: Rules for player characters conferring a commanding aura on others through an investiture ceremony.

entries.title: Sabbat Politics
entries.summary: Four optional ways a sabbat can run (Easy, Bickering, Dictatorial, Feuding), depending on the Gifted makeup of the coven and the kind of stories wanted.

entries.title: Hermetic Courtesy and Hospitality
entries.summary: Jerbiton code of conduct listing the obligations of guests and hosts when visiting another Jerbiton magus's territory; breaking it is taken as a deliberate insult.
quotes: It is rude to refuse to offer hospitality, but it is also rude to demand it.

entries.title: Epistolary Community (Gifted mathematici and correspondence)
entries.summary: Gifted mathematici use long correspondence to overcome the social effects of The Gift, and a successful Communication plus Charm roll can let a face-to-face meeting count as an established relationship instead of a first impression.
quotes: successful in a Communication + Charm roll against an Ease Factor set by the storyguide

related.text: ArM5 p.76 First Impression and Established Relationship

entries.title: Nothing Grows for the Wicked
entries.requires: Optional folkloric rule chosen by the troupe
entries.summary: An optional folkloric approach in which virtuous, successful characters are blessed with good harvests and community loyalty, replacing the annual harvest roll.
quotes: Troupes using this system select good harvests rather than making the annual roll called for by the Mythic Pound system (see Covenants).

entries.title: Offices
entries.summary: Explains what an officer of a lord is, how officers differ from hereditary vassals, what their underlings will and will not do, and that characters built as officers need the Temporal Influence Virtue. The individual offices that follow are descriptive.
quotes: Characters designed as officers need the Temporal Influence Virtue.

entries.title: Improvement in Living Standards
entries.summary: Introduces the sinful ways peasants increase their wealth, which make a character richer than pious neighbors.
quotes: Characters performing any of these sins will be substantially wealthier than their more pious neighbors

entries.title: Social Penalty of the Gift (hedge traditions)
entries.summary: Gifted hedge wizards suffer the Gift's social penalty even with other Gifted characters unless their tradition has found a remedy comparable to Parma Magica.

entries.title: The Economics of Tithing
entries.summary: How heavy tithing is for a peasant and the traditional four-way division of tithes among rector, curate, church fabric and the poor.
quotes: Tithing effectively swallows twenty percent of the income of most peasants.
One-quarter of all tithes go to the rector of the manor.

entries.title: Town Officials as a Virtue
entries.requires: Optional rule: Town Magistrate Social Status Virtue
entries.summary: Advises treating town office as part of a story, but offers a variant of the Town Magistrate Virtue for a general town official, with the Civil and Canon Law requirement and Academic Abilities benefit dropped.
quotes: a Virtue modeled upon the Minor Social Status Virtue: Town Magistrate (see Crime) can be used

entries.title: Trial by Ordeal
entries.requires: Defendant found guilty who insists on innocence
entries.summary: Summarises the four trials by ordeal (combat, cold water, hot water, iron) and what counts as proof of innocence in each.
quotes: A defendant who insists his innocence, even when the court finds him guilty, can choose to undergo a trial by ordeal.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.78

entries.title: Saintly Reputation
entries.summary: Miracles raise a saintly character's Reputation quickly, and a character with a True Faith Score cannot gain a negative Reputation.
quotes: Each miracle he successfully prays for counts as one noteworthy action per Faith Point he possesses, so long as there was a witness.

entries.title: Usurers (High-Interest Lending)
entries.summary: Describes higher interest rates charged by lenders who disregard the charge of usury, the social consequences, and advice for building a character who is an Usurer, including recommended Flaws and the Profession: Accountant Ability.
quotes: might ask closer to 50% interest on common loans
